title: UK retail sales, Great Britain — November 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the Black Friday month's first estimate, landing pre-dawn on US quad-witching Friday
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/retailsalesgreatbritainnovember2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 42,021 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Retail sales, Great Britain: November 2026', 'Release date: 18 December 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', summary 'A first estimate of retail sales in volume and value terms, seasonally and non-seasonally adjusted', with the Office for Statistics Regulation accredited-official-statistics statement on the release page. Cadence corroborated from the publisher's own JSON bulletin index (api.beta.ons.gov.uk, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200): 137 retail-sales bulletins are indexed, and the eleven November-edition bulletins printed on 2015-12-17, 2016-12-15, 2017-12-14, 2018-12-20, 2019-12-19, 2020-12-18, 2021-12-17, 2022-12-16, 2023-12-22, 2024-12-20 and 2025-12-19 — a 14-22 December band that contains 2026-12-18. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-public-sector-finances-2026-12-22 LANE, 2026-09-09, discovered in that event's adjacency sweep of the ONS upcoming-release index across 17-29 December 2026. Two reasons it earns a slot rather than being noted and dropped. First, a series gap: this calendar tracks US retail-sales prints monthly (retail-sales-2026-09-16 through -2026-12-16) and carries the UK series only as a single proposal for a different date (uk-retail-sales-2026-10-23.from-uk-ppi-2026-10-21), so the UK consumer read for the peak trading month is currently invisible while its US counterpart is not. Second, and the reason it belongs in THIS lane's corridor specifically: 2026-12-18 is US quad-witching (opex-2026-12-18, confirmed, high) — so a 02:00 ET UK consumer print opens the same session as the year's densest US derivatives expiry, which is an attribution hazard of exactly the kind this lane's parent event documents for 2026-12-22. The November edition is also the Black Friday month's FIRST estimate, the single noisiest month for seasonal adjustment in the series. Tiered LOW and symbols [] because this repo tracks no UK-listed name and no house playbook is consumer-, sterling- or rates-keyed; the tier is a statement about this book's instruments, not about the print's importance to a UK-facing one. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
